51416912.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to full length CIB1 (unknown origin) at 300 uM by isothermal titration calorimetry
51416912.references_previous: Puhl, A. C.; Bogart, J. W.; Haberman, V. A.; Larson, J. E.; Godoy, A. S.; Norris-Drouin, J. L.; Cholensky, S. H.; Leisner, T. M.; Frye, S. V.; Parise, L. V.; Bowers, A. A.; Pearce, K. H. Discovery and Characterization of Peptide Inhibitors for Calcium and Integrin Binding Protein 1. ACS Chem. Biol. 2020, 15 (6), 1505–1516. https://doi.org/10.1021/acschembio.0c00144.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Isothermal Calor: ITC with full-length CIB1 was performed as previously described.6 Briefly, CIB1 was diluted to a final concentration of 30 μM in 50 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 0.1 mM CaCl2. UNC10245131 was dissolved in the same buffer at a final concentration of 300 μM. ITC measurements were recorded using an AutoITC 200 microcalorimeter (Malvern Instruments) at 25 °C. Peptides were titrated into a 200 μL well containing CIB1 protein at 0.2 μL/injection, with a spacing of 180 seconds, and a reference power of 7 μcal/s. As control, peptide was titrated into buffer alone under identical conditions to determine heats of dilution and then subtracted from the protein-peptide binding curve. The ITC data were analyzed using Origin Software (Malvern Instruments) and were fitted using a nonlinear least-squares, the heats of binding were fitted as a function of the peptide-protein ratio to a one site binding model.
